panels.sample_scope: Fig. 10 | Supported initial shear shifts show a clearer recovery contrast than humidity shifts. Recovery modelling uses the first eligible historical-threshold departure in 2,231 SIDs with valid model inputs from the 2,340-SID main sample. Policies reduce initial 200–850 hPa shear by 2 m s⁻¹ or increase initial mean 700/500 hPa relative humidity (RH) by 5 percentage points where both exposures satisfy training-fold support; other exposures are unchanged. a,b, Policy-minus-natural-course differences in recovery within 48 h and wind change over 24 h, respectively. Symbols distinguish g-formula, one-step augmented and density-weighted estimates; bars are 95% percentile intervals from 1,000 complete cyclone-level bootstrap refits. Higher wind-change contrasts include slower weakening. c, Changed-exposure fraction and density-ratio effective sample size (ESS) divided by the 2,231-cyclone model-subset size. Density ratios give . ESS measures weight concentration, not the number of recoveries. d, G-formula recovery contrasts under policy-specific log-odds offsets for changed cyclones with missing outcomes. Zero is the fitted missing-at-random model; unchanged cyclones retain zero policy contrast. Curves show fixed response assumptions without confidence intervals. pp, percentage points; kt, knots.
